title: What you used to do
description: Describe the past, the way it really was.
grammarNote: The imperfect ends in -aba for -ar verbs and -ía for -er and -ir verbs.

explanation.summary: Spanish has two past tenses and the difference is about the camera, not the clock. The preterite says something happened at a moment. The imperfect says how things were, or what used to happen.

sections.heading: The two pasts
sections.body: The preterite is for a completed event: Ayer hablé con mi madre. The imperfect is for a background: De niño Jugaba en el parque. When a past event is interrupted by another past event, the interrupted one is imperfect: Leía cuando llamó. When one past event interrupts another, the interrupting one is preterite: Leía cuando llamó — the call is the interruption.

examples.en: Yesterday I spoke to my mother.

examples.es: De niño jugaba en el parque.
examples.en: As a child I used to play in the park.
I was sleeping when the phone rang.

sections.heading: How the forms are built
sections.body: For -ar verbs the imperfect ends in -aba: hablar, hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban. For -er and -ir verbs it ends in -ía: comer, comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían. There are only three irregular verbs in the imperfect: ser was era, ir went iba, and ver saw veía.

sections.heading: The one-liner
sections.body: The imperfect is for things you cannot put a time on: how things were, what you used to do, what you were doing. The preterite is for things that happened.

items.note: The imperfect of hablar. It describes how things were.
The imperfect of comer. It describes how things were.
The imperfect of vivir. It describes how things were.
The imperfect of ser. It is irregular, like ir and ver.
